correctness.rationale: For each x in P1∩P2, the fiber is a sum of scaled intervals, so its length is θℓ1(x)+(1−θ)ℓ2(x). Fubini gives the area identity. Subtraction from θ area(K1)+(1−θ) area(K2) yields the displayed nonnegative deficit. For full-dimensional planar convex bodies, each fiber length is positive on the interior of its projection interval, so the deficit vanishes iff P1=P2. The rectangle example is exact: areas 4, 8, and 4, against a printed lower bound of 6.
